sections.h2: How can I sell a house fast in Walla Walla, WA?
sections.html:
The quickest routes are a sale to a cash buyer or an as-is sale to an investor, because neither waits on a mortgage approval. A standard listing can still make sense if the house is in good shape, but it comes with showings, an appraisal and the buyer's loan timeline.

Walla Walla is the county seat of Walla Walla County, set in a valley in southeastern Washington about 6 miles north of the Oregon line. The city is compact, covering roughly 13 square miles, and it sits near College Place, which adds a second small city to the same housing market.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers show for Walla Walla homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page for Walla Walla gives a picture of the local housing stock and household base.

The population is nearly flat, so a seller should expect buyers to compare your house closely with others on the market rather than assume rising demand will carry it. The short commute, under 13 minutes on average, is a real asset when you describe the location.

sections.h2: What drives the Walla Walla economy and housing demand?
sections.html:
Agriculture, wine, education and corrections anchor the local economy. Wheat remains a significant crop, and the wine boom of the past three decades produced more than 120 wineries in the greater Walla Walla area by summer 2020. The Walla Walla Sweet Onion is Washington's official state vegetable and has its own festival each July.

  • Whitman College, an independent liberal arts college in the city
  • Walla Walla Community College, which has a winemaking and grape growing program
  • Walla Walla University in nearby College Place
  • Washington State Penitentiary, opened in 1886, with about 2,000 inmates and about 1,000 staff

The city began as Steptoeville in 1856 around Fort Walla Walla and was incorporated on January 11, 1862, so older neighborhoods near downtown carry a long building history. The 13-story Marcus Whitman Hotel, which opened in 1928, is the tallest building in the city.

sections.h2: How does Walla Walla's climate affect a house?
sections.html:
Walla Walla lies in the rain shadow of the Cascades, so annual precipitation is fairly low. It has a hot-summer Mediterranean climate, yet winters can still turn cold. The valley's grape growers know the risk well: a killing freeze hits about once every six or seven years.

The city's building permitting page sets technical design numbers that any repair or addition must meet:

  • Ground and minimum roof snow load of 30 pounds per square foot
  • Design wind speed of 110 mph
  • Seismic design category D
  • Frost depth of 24 inches
  • Ice shield underlayment required

If you have replaced a roof or added a structure, keep the permit paperwork to hand over at closing.

sections.h2: Which schools and roads matter to Walla Walla buyers?
sections.html:
Most of the city belongs to Walla Walla Public Schools, which runs seven elementary schools, two middle schools, one traditional high school (Wa-Hi) and two alternative high schools, Lincoln and Opportunity. The far western edge of the city is in the College Place School District. Private options include the Walla Walla Catholic Schools, with Assumption K-8 and DeSales High School, and several Christian schools.

U.S. Route 12 is the main east-west highway, and since 2003 the Washington State Department of Transportation has expanded it to four lanes between Pasco and Walla Walla, with the eighth section finished in June 2023. State Route 125 runs through town and into Milton-Freewater, Oregon. Valley Transit serves Walla Walla and College Place and has been fare-free since 2022, and the Walla Walla Regional Airport has commercial flights to Seattle-Tacoma twice a day.

sections.h2: Do I need a permit to fix up a Walla Walla house before selling?
sections.html:
If the work is structural, mechanical or plumbing related, yes, the city handles it through Development Services. The department issues permits and inspections for new construction, remodels, mechanical and plumbing work, signs and other land use activity inside city limits, and it adopted the 2021 International Building Codes.

Applications, payments and inspection requests moved online for permits processed after August 19, 2025. Older permits may still involve contact with the permit technicians for payment and inspections. For a project that is not clearly listed, ask Development Services before you start.

sections.h2: What if my Walla Walla house is a short-term rental?
sections.html:
The rules depend on which type of short-term rental you have. According to the city's short-term rental FAQ, a Type 1 rental is the owner's principal residence, either with rooms rented while the owner is present or the entire dwelling rented no more than 90 days a year. A Type 2 rental is a dwelling that is not the owner's principal residence.

City Council adopted Ordinance 2017-33, which bans new Type 2 rentals. Those that were lawfully operating before November 9, 2017 may continue as non-conforming uses, and that status runs with the property if the use has not been abandoned. A buyer of such a property must obtain a Type 2 permit and license at closing, with proof of ownership. The permit can be lost in several ways:

  • Use is presumed abandoned if the location was not rented at least a total of 29 days in the preceding year
  • Use ends if the location sits unrented for 6 consecutive months or more
  • A fourth nuisance violation leads to revocation, after fines of $750 and then $1,000

If you own a Type 2 rental, ask Development Services for the current permit status before you advertise the sale, since a buyer's offer may depend on it.

sections.h2: How is a deed handled in Walla Walla County?
sections.html:
RCW 82.45.090 puts the real estate excise tax in the hands of the treasurer of the county where the property sits, who acts as the state's agent. The county auditor then has no authority to take the deed for recording until payment is verified or the treasurer notes that nothing is due. In Walla Walla County that means a visit or mailing to the Treasurer first, then recording through the Auditor.

Ask the Walla Walla County Treasurer for the total excise tax at your sale price, since the tax combines a state and a local portion. A title or escrow company normally carries the affidavit and deed through both offices for you.

The seller also owes a written condition disclosure. RCW 64.06.020 prescribes the form for improved residential property, and the delivery deadline is five business days after a signed purchase contract, absent a different agreement. Receiving it gives the buyer three business days to back out.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Walla Walla house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Investors and cash buyers often take houses with deferred maintenance. The seller disclosure form under RCW 64.06.020 still has to go to the buyer, and known defects or unpermitted work belong on it.

faqs.q: Can a new owner keep running my Walla Walla house as a short-term rental?
faqs.a: Only in limited cases. New Type 2 rentals are banned, but a lawfully established one that has not been abandoned keeps its non-conforming status with the property. The new owner must obtain a Type 2 permit and license at closing with proof of ownership.

faqs.q: What building design numbers apply to Walla Walla houses?
faqs.a: The city lists a 30 pound per square foot roof snow load, a 110 mph wind speed, seismic design category D and a 24 inch frost depth. Ice shield underlayment is also required. These apply to new work under the 2021 International Building Codes.

faqs.q: Who collects the excise tax when a Walla Walla house sells?
faqs.a: The county treasurer, acting as the state's agent under RCW 82.45.090. Recording waits until the tax is paid or noted as not due, so ask the Walla Walla County Treasurer for the figure at your price.

faqs.q: Which school district serves my Walla Walla address?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in Walla Walla Public Schools. The extreme western edge is in the College Place School District. Verify the boundary with the district for your street.
